title: UK PPI — September 2026, including services July to September 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the quarterly SPPI print, and the only three-release ONS minute this calendar tracks
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/producerpriceinflationukseptember2026includingservicesjulytoseptember2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'Producer price inflation, UK: September 2026 including services, July to September 2026', '21 October 2026 at 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', and describes contents including 'quarterly data on price changes for specified services rendered by British businesses'. The quarterly services cadence is independently reproduced from the publisher's own previous-releases listing (fetched direct 2026-09-09): 'including services' appears on the December 2025 (released 21 January 2026), March 2026 (22 April 2026) and June 2026 (22 July 2026) reference months and on no others in the visible listing — the Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec rule. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: and no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics.
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding proposals/uk-ppi-2026-10-21.from-uk-ppi-2026-11-18.json (read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md). BOTH OF THE PROPOSAL'S FINDINGS SURVIVE AND ONE IS SHARPENED. Sharpened: the proposal called this 'the same-minute twin' of uk-cpi-2026-10-21, inheriting the sibling ledger's two-release rule. Three ONS release pages fetched direct today all read 7:00am on 21 October 2026 — Producer price inflation, Consumer price inflation AND Public sector finances. 2026-10-21 is the only THREE-release 02:00 ET ONS slot this calendar tracks (11-18 pairs CPI+PPI with PSF on 11-20; 09-16 and 12-16 pair CPI+PPI with PSF on 09-22 and 12-22 respectively). Any 02:00 ET UK move that morning has three candidate causes, not two. WHAT THIS ENTRY ADDS THAT ITS GOODS SIBLING CANNOT: the services half. SPPI facts, all from the publisher, fetched 2026-09-09 — designated 'official statistics', NOT accredited; the QMI calls it 'a partial, best estimate of the overall inflation to UK businesses from the services sector' with 'limited coverage of the services sector because of data collection challenges'; nine product groups; 'the last two quarters are provisional and the last five quarters are subject to revisions'; weighted response rate 77.1% in Q2 2026, down from 83.0% a year earlier; Q1/Q2 2025 SPPI publications cancelled after a chain-linking methodology error found in March 2025, corrections applied retrospectively to 2014. THE SERIES AND THE CALL: SPPI y/y ran 2.0% (Q3 2025, revised from 2.1%) -> 2.9% (Q4) -> 3.0% (Q1 2026) -> 4.3% (Q2 2026), q/q 0.7 / 0.7 / 0.8 / 1.8. Base case: the four-quarter acceleration STALLS at 3.9-4.9% y/y, centred ~4.4%, because Q2's 1.8% was one non-repeating group — transportation and storage rose 7.3% q/q, which the bulletin itself calls 'the highest the quarterly rate has been for this product group since records began in Quarter 4 (Oct to Dec) 2008', on 'increased shipping rates and fuel charges resulting from the conflict in the Middle East' — and quarterly-average Brent in sterling FELL 7.8% from Q2 to Q3 2026 (computed from Yahoo BZ=F x GBPUSD=X, fetched). THE GOODS HALF IS ALREADY DETERMINED: per the PPI QMI, firms price 'transactions that occur on or near to the first of each month', so the September 2026 index priced around 1 September 2026 — a date already past. First-week Brent in sterling ran +12.0% m/m in August and +16.3% in September against a flat 2025 base (Aug/Sep m/m 0.0/0.0), which at crude's 6.9% input weight puts the September input annual rate near 7.0% against 4.9% in July. This print is therefore the first test of the sibling's Brent->PPI model with NO forward price risk left in it. Tiered LOW on the same measured grounds as every UK sibling: symbols: [], no rates-, fiscal- or sterling-keyed house playbook, no UK-listed name in this book.
